title: Local Agent authority lifecycle
summary: How the Electron-owned structured Agent authority verifies and recovers durable state, remains usable without a window, fails closed into terminal-only safe mode, and drains before SQLite closes.

chapters.title: Crash-safe startup
chapters.summary: Existing material is contained, backed up when required, migrated, and reconciled before structured clients can observe ready state.

chapters.title: Terminal-only safe mode
chapters.summary: Unsafe, future, corrupt, or unverified database state disables structured Agent mutation for the process lifetime while preserving legacy terminal access.

chapters.title: Optional window lifetime
chapters.summary: With keep-running enabled, closing the workbench hides the window while the Electron-main authority continues to own work.

chapters.title: Ordered shutdown
chapters.summary: Quit closes ingress, drains accepted commands and automation, persists Agent termination when legal, releases providers and MCP, then closes the store.

states.label: Persisted daemon material
states.detail: SQLite, WAL sidecars, and named legacy sources remain under one contained user-data recovery boundary.

evidence.claim: DaemonStoreRecovery owns the contained filesystem boundary for exact SQLite material and explicitly named legacy inputs.

states.label: Verifying and recovering store
states.detail: Containment, integrity, backup, schema migration, and uncertain-command recovery must finish before the store becomes ready.

evidence.claim: Initialization validates containment and existing database material, rejects future schemas, and requires a verified migration or legacy backup before mutation.
The store opens with strict SQLite options, enables WAL and full synchronization, migrates, recovers uncertain commands, then marks itself ready.

states.label: Structured authority ready
states.detail: The router, session MCP, provider state machine, automation, and revisioned projections are live; the workbench is only one client.

evidence.claim: Only after store and lifecycle initialization does main synchronize settings, start MCP, rehydrate Agents, start automation, and bind shutdown to startup.
Agent startup restores provider subscriptions, expires approvals, repairs claims, rehydrates Sessions, reconciles unsettled work, and rearms durable timeouts.

states.label: Terminal-only safe mode
states.detail: The failure and database disposition are latched; structured Agent reads and writes stop while legacy terminal operation remains available.

evidence.claim: Any structured-store initialization error becomes a stable legacy-only safe-mode availability record with its database disposition.
Desktop clients can still read availability, while structured snapshot and command paths return unavailable or reject with the terminal-only safe-mode reason.
Main reports structured authority failure as a terminal-preserving safe mode rather than failing the entire desktop runtime.

states.label: Window hidden, daemon running
states.detail: With explicit keep-running preference, closing the main window hides it without ending provider or terminal processes.

evidence.claim: The main-window close policy hides only when keepRunning is enabled; opening restores, shows, and focuses the same authority client window.

states.label: Ingress closed and draining
states.detail: New commands and provider probes stop synchronously while accepted FIFO work, startup, automation, Agents, and MCP settle exactly once.

evidence.claim: The idempotent authority barrier closes command, provider, and Agent ingress first, then drains automation, startup, Agent persistence, and both early and late MCP instances.

states.label: Authority and SQLite closed
states.detail: The store closes only after the exact authority barrier and concurrent desktop writers have drained.

evidence.claim: The close helper awaits the exact authority stop plus every concurrent drain before preparing and closing the store.
Main joins the authority, daemon runtime, and desktop-file drains before removing event fanout and closing DaemonStore.
DaemonStore serializes initialization, latches a structured failure, and never exposes a partially initialized database.
Successful database and lifecycle initialization gates the ordered start of every structured Agent runtime.
A rejected store initialization is converted once into process-lifetime safe-mode availability and logged without blocking legacy store initialization.
Closing the main window hides it only when keepRunning is true; otherwise the same event requests application Quit.
Reopening creates a missing window or restores, shows, and focuses the existing renderer client.
Quit immediately closes external ingress and begins Agent shutdown before awaiting the exact drain sequence.
Explicit Quit requests application shutdown, whose process owner stops all registered daemon resources exactly once.
When no writable authority exists, safe-mode shutdown selects process-loss cleanup so it releases providers without attempting structured database writes.
SQLite closure cannot run until the authoritative stop promise and all concurrent writer drains resolve.
